record.paper_title: A List of Problems on the Reverse Mathematics of Ramsey Theory on the Rado Graph and on Infinite, Finitely Branching Trees
record.original_question: Does the rainbow Ramsey theorem for the Rado graph have the same reverse-mathematical strength as the canonical partition theorem of Sauer for colorings of a fixed finite graph inside the Rado graph?

evidence.quote: (C) Canonical partition theorem on colorings of a fixed finite graph inside the Rado graph.
(11) Does the rainbow Ramsey theorem for the Rado graph have the same reverse math strength as the canonical partition theorem of Sauer?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions:

- The Rado graph R is the unique (up to isomorphism) countable graph that is universal and ultrahomogeneous for finite graphs; equivalently, it satisfies the extension property: for any two disjoint finite sets U, V of vertices, there is a vertex adjacent to every vertex of U and to no vertex of V.

- For a finite graph A, an embedding of A into R is an injective map of vertices preserving the edge and non-edge relations. Write Emb(A, R) for the set of all such embeddings (equivalently, the set of induced copies of A in R).

- Sauer's canonical partition theorem (for the Rado graph): For every finite graph A there is a finite number t(A) and a partition of Emb(A, R) into t(A) canonical classes such that, for every finite coloring c of Emb(A, R), there exists an induced copy R' of R inside R on which c, restricted to Emb(A, R'), takes at most t(A) values, with each value coming from one of the canonical classes. Call this statement CPT(A), and let CPT denote the statement "for all finite graphs A, CPT(A) holds."

- The rainbow Ramsey theorem for the Rado graph, denoted RRT(R): For every finite graph A, and every coloring c: Emb(A, R) → ω such that each color class is finite (i.e., c uses each color only finitely often), there exists an induced copy R' of R in R on which c is injective on Emb(A, R').

- Reverse mathematics: working over the base system RCA_0 (recursive comprehension axiom), one compares the proof-theoretic / computability-theoretic strength of mathematical statements by determining which implications between them are provable in RCA_0, and to which standard subsystems (such as ACA_0, ACA_0', etc.) they are equivalent.

Problem: Determine whether the rainbow Ramsey theorem RRT(R) for the Rado graph and Sauer's canonical partition theorem CPT for finite graphs inside the Rado graph have the same reverse-mathematical strength. That is, are RRT(R) and CPT equivalent over RCA_0 (or some other natural base theory), or does one strictly imply the other?
artifact.category_tag: Reverse mathematics of Ramsey theory on the Rado graph
artifact.status_search_result: A web search reveals active research on rainbow Ramsey-type theorems and canonical Ramsey results, including reverse-mathematical investigations of rainbow Ramsey for pairs (which is known to be strictly weaker than Ramsey's theorem for pairs over RCA_0) and combinatorial work on Rado-graph partition theorems by Laflamme–Sauer–Vuksanovic. However, no source directly establishes or refutes a reverse-mathematical equivalence between the rainbow Ramsey theorem for the Rado graph and Sauer's canonical partition theorem. The question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: The Strength of the Rainbow Ramsey Theorem
status_evidence.snippet: Rainbow Ramsey Theorem for pairs is strictly weaker than Ramsey's Theorem for pairs over RCA_0.
status_evidence.claim: Reverse-mathematical analyses of rainbow Ramsey statements are active, but no equivalence with Sauer's canonical partition theorem on the Rado graph is established.

status_evidence.title: Rainbow Ramsey Simple Structures
status_evidence.snippet: The Rado graph is Rainbow Ramsey but not Ramsey.
status_evidence.claim: Rainbow Ramsey behavior on the Rado graph is studied combinatorially, without resolving its reverse-math strength versus Sauer's theorem.

status_evidence.title: Ramsey Theory for Countable Binary Homogeneous Structures
status_evidence.snippet: Partition theorem of Laflamme, Sauer, and Vuksanovic for countable homogeneous binary relational structures.
status_evidence.claim: Sauer-type canonical partition theorems are studied, but a precise reverse-math comparison with the rainbow Ramsey theorem for the Rado graph is not given.
